name: Hirefrank
tagline: An AI agent that works your job pipeline: tailoring applications, matching roles, keeping track of where everything stands.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The language-model half of this is genuinely easy now: feeding a resume and a job description to a model and getting back a tailored version, a cover letter, and a gap analysis is a one-sitting build. The hard half is supply, the stream of fresh, deduplicated, actually-open roles, because job boards rate limit, block scrapers, and rot within days. A personal build works fine if you are willing to paste postings in yourself or point it at feeds you already have legitimate access to. You also lose the nagging: a product that emails you reminders and keeps a queue warm beats a local script you forget to run. Build it if your bottleneck is writing applications, pay if your bottleneck is finding them.
coreLoopDIY: A local app where you paste a job posting, it scores fit against your resume, drafts a tailored resume and cover letter, and tracks the application through stages.
requirements: An LLM API key (Anthropic or OpenAI)
Your resume as text or Markdown
Node 20 and local disk; no hosting required
Patience for pasting postings, or a feed you already have access to
whatYouLose: Automated job discovery: no crawler, no deduplicated feed, no alerts on new postings
Any recruiter-side or employer network the hosted product may have
Email and calendar nudges that keep you applying when motivation dips
Polished export formats and ATS-safe resume templates that someone else already debugged
Mobile access, unless you host the thing yourself
moatNotes: The defensible asset in job-search tooling is almost never the prompt, it is the fresh posting index and whatever employer relationships sit behind it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the job hunt is an energy problem, not a text generation problem. People pay for something that shows up with five relevant roles on a Tuesday morning, remembers that they never followed up on the third one, and makes the next step one click instead of a context switch into a side project they built and abandoned. A local script does the writing well and the discipline badly.
notes: The drafting is commoditized; the pipeline of live, real openings is not.
prompt:
Build a local job application workbench. Stack: Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, and the Anthropic SDK. Single user, runs on localhost, no auth, no telemetry, no cloud services.

Setup:
- Read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .env.local. Ship .env.example. Never hardcode keys.
- SQLite file at ./data/jobs.db, created and migrated on first boot.
- Tables: profile (one row: resume_markdown, highlights, constraints), jobs (company, title, url, posting_text, status, fit_score, fit_notes, created_at), artifacts (job_id, kind, content, created_at), events (job_id, note, created_at).

Features, in scope:
1. Profile page: paste resume as Markdown plus freeform notes on what you want and will not accept. Stored locally.
2. Add Job page: paste a posting URL and the raw posting text. Do not scrape; a server action may fetch the URL and strip tags as a best effort, and must fail gracefully back to manual paste.
3. On save, call Claude once to return strict JSON: fit_score 0-100, three reasons for, three reasons against, missing keywords, and two questions to ask the interviewer. Persist it. Show the raw JSON behind a toggle.
4. Job detail page: buttons to generate a tailored resume (Markdown, reordered and reworded from the profile, no invented employers, dates, or credentials) and a cover letter under 250 words. Store each as an artifact with a timestamp so older versions stay readable.
5. Kanban board across statuses: saved, applied, screening, onsite, offer, rejected. Drag to move, which writes an event row.
6. Dashboard: counts by status, jobs with no activity in 7+ days, median fit score.
7. Export: one button writing every job, artifact, and event to ./export as Markdown files.

Out of scope, do not build: job scraping or aggregation, email sending, browser extensions, autofill of external application forms, multi-user accounts, payments, PDF rendering beyond the browser print stylesheet.

Honesty requirements: prompts must instruct the model to refuse to fabricate experience, and the UI must label all generated text as a draft. If an LLM call fails, show the error, do not fake a result.

Deliver a README with setup in under five commands and a seed script that inserts two fake postings so the board is not empty on first run.
